result.question: I'd rather take Transformer 1 at site MAIN out of service once than three times. Pull every open and pending-approval work order on it. For each one, give me the number, description, priority and scheduled date, and say whether it needs the unit de-energized, for example internal inspection, OLTC work or electrical testing, or whether it can be done live, for example oil sampling. Group the outage-needing work orders into bundles. Each bundle must have at least two work orders whose scheduled dates fall within 14 days of each other. For each bundle, propose a single outage date where the MAIN calendar has the fewest other scheduled work orders. Estimate each bundle's total planned hours, using the planned hours on the work orders themselves. Where a work order has no plan, use the average actual hours of closed work orders on Transformer 1. Then check the latest acetylene and hydrogen. If acetylene is above 1 ppm, any bundle with OLTC or inspection work moves to the earliest possible date regardless of calendar load. If fewer than two outage-needing work orders exist, don't bundle anything. Recommend whether each one should be done alone or deferred to the next planned outage, and why.
result.answer:
I found two Transformer 1 work orders, both waiting for approval (WAPPR). Two of your rules can't be applied as written: no bundle qualifies under the 14-day rule, and there are no planned hours to total.

**Work orders**

| WO | Description | Priority | Scheduled date | Needs de-energizing? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection, on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking) | 1 | None set. The notes give a target start of **2024-01-19**, which is 2½ years ago. | **Yes.** Inspecting the tap changer's contacts means taking the unit out of service. |
| 1000052 | Oil sample retest (DGA) and insulation check for a T2 thermal fault | 3 | None set. The notes give a target start of **2026-10-01**. | **Partly.** The oil sample can be taken live, but the insulation check (insulation resistance / PI testing) needs the unit de-energized. |

Neither work order has a formal scheduled date; I used the target dates written in their notes.

**Bundling: no bundle qualifies under your rule**
- Both work orders involve outage work, so the "fewer than two" rule doesn't apply.
- But their dates are about 2.7 years apart (2024-01-19 vs 2026-10-01), not within 14 days, so I haven't formed a bundle.
- **Hours:** neither work order has planned hours. The fallback doesn't work either: these are the only two work orders on Transformer 1 and neither is closed, so there are no actual hours to average. Hours can't be estimated from the data.

**Latest gas readings (2024-01-19)**
- Acetylene is **7 ppm**, above your 1 ppm trigger.
- Hydrogen is **2,850 ppm**, with ethylene at 16,650 ppm and methane at 7,400 ppm. This fits a severe thermal fault.
- These readings are more than 2½ years old. Take a fresh oil sample now to confirm them.
- Because acetylene is over 1 ppm, the OLTC inspection moves to the earliest possible date. The MAIN calendar has **no work orders scheduled from 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-31**, so the earliest workable date is **2026-10-01**.

**Recommendations**
- **1000051 (OLTC):** don't defer it. Transformer 1 has no other planned outage to defer it to, and the acetylene reading is high. Do it on 2026-10-01; its 2024 target date is overdue.
- **1000052 (DGA and insulation check):** take the oil sample live right away. Its target date is also 2026-10-01, so do the insulation check during the same outage as 1000051.

That shared date means one outage covers both jobs, which is what you wanted. It's a practical merge, not a bundle under your 14-day rule. Both work orders still need approval, and planned hours should be added before the outage is booked.

details.suggestions: The agent used the correct asset (Transformer 1), site (MAIN), gas sensors (acetylene/hydrogen via iot.latest_reading) and the MAIN schedule calendar, and its outage-vs-live classification, 14-day bundling logic, acetylene>1 ppm expedite rule and standalone/defer recommendations are reasonable and clearly explained. However, the expected workflow was not fully executed: it never called wo.get_workorder or wo.get_workorder_tasks to confirm scope/planned hours per work order, and it never called wo.get_workorder_actuals_vs_planned to attempt the fallback average from closed Transformer 1 work orders, instead asserting from the list alone that no closed work orders exist. The list_workorders output is not captured in the trace, so the detailed notes/target dates the agent cites cannot be independently verified; it should have fetched each work order explicitly. It also queried only a one-month calendar window, and the claim that a 2024 target date is 'not within 14 days' of the 2026 date is technically true but an overdue WO should arguably be treated as immediately schedulable, which the agent effectively did anyway via the 'practical merge' — the response would be cleaner if it stated that the overdue WO collapses to today and therefore the two do form a bundle.
